If you contributed camera trap data to WildObs, you will want to know what others now see:
which of your projects are listed, what their metadata say, when embargoed data will be
released, and how people will cite you. This vignette answers those questions with the same
public API key everyone uses. Here we use the package maintainer's projects as the example;
put your own name, email or ORCID in their place.


``` r
library(WildObsR)

# your personal API key, read from .Renviron (see the Get started vignette)
api_key <- Sys.getenv("WILDOBSR_API_KEY")
```

## Find your projects

The `contributors` filter matches anyone listed on a project, in any role. Give a full name,
an email address or an ORCID; mixing them catches projects where you were listed
differently:


``` r
# projects listing this person, by name or ORCID
mine <- wildobs_mongo_query(api_key = api_key,
                            contributors = c("Zachary Amir", "0000-0002-8398-2059"))
mine
#> [1] "QLD_Dwyers_Scrub_ANIM3018_2023_WildObsID_0005"
#> [2] "QLD_Kgari_BIOL2015_2023-24_WildObsID_0004"    
#> [3] "QLD_Kgari_potoroos_Amir_2022_WildObsID_0003"  
#> [4] "ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001"
```

## Check how your projects are described

The metadata are what people read first, and what they cite. Download them alone, which
takes seconds, and check that the contributors, roles, organisations and licences are right:


``` r
# the descriptors of your projects, without their tables
meta <- wildobs_dp_download(api_key = api_key, project_ids = mine, metadata_only = TRUE)
#> metadata_only = TRUE -> skipping data resource downloads for speed.

# who is credited on each project, and in what role
contributors <- extract_metadata(meta, "contributors")
contributors[, c("title", "role", "DPID")]
#>                title                  role
#> 1       Zachary Amir principalInvestigator
#> 2      Annabel Smith          rightsHolder
#> 3       Zachary Amir principalInvestigator
#> 4     Matthew Luskin          rightsHolder

#> 6   Steven Salisbury           contributor

#> 10      Zachary Amir principalInvestigator
#> 11         Tom Bruce               contact
#> 12    Matthew Luskin          rightsHolder
#>                                             DPID
#> 1  QLD_Dwyers_Scrub_ANIM3018_2023_WildObsID_0005
#> 2  QLD_Dwyers_Scrub_ANIM3018_2023_WildObsID_0005
#> 3      QLD_Kgari_BIOL2015_2023-24_WildObsID_0004
#> 4      QLD_Kgari_BIOL2015_2023-24_WildObsID_0004
```

If something is wrong, contact WildObs at <support@wildobs.org.au> rather than editing a
download: the database is the record everyone else reads.

## Know when embargoed data are released

A project shared as `partial` lists its metadata but withholds its tables until its embargo
ends. The embargo runs for `embargoPeriodMonths` from the project's `created` date, and the
tables are released at the next database update after that:


``` r
# sharing preference and embargo length for each project
sharing <- extract_metadata(meta, "WildObsMetadata")
# the date each project was created
created <- vapply(meta, function(dp) substr(dp$created, 1, 10), character(1))

# the earliest date each embargo can end
data.frame(
  project = sharing$DPID,
  sharing = sharing$tabularSharingPreference,
  embargo_months = sharing$embargoPeriodMonths,
  embargo_ends = as.Date(created[sharing$DPID]) + round(sharing$embargoPeriodMonths * 30.44),
  row.names = NULL
)
#>                                         project sharing embargo_months
#> 1 QLD_Dwyers_Scrub_ANIM3018_2023_WildObsID_0005    open              0
#> 2     QLD_Kgari_BIOL2015_2023-24_WildObsID_0004 partial             16
#> 3   QLD_Kgari_potoroos_Amir_2022_WildObsID_0003    open              0
#> 4     ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001    open              0
#>   embargo_ends
#> 1   2024-12-06
#> 2   2027-04-10
#> 3   2024-11-06
#> 4   2025-02-18
```

## See your data as others do

A public key returns your open projects exactly as anyone else receives them, which differs
from what you uploaded in three ways:

- **Threatened species are obscured** in the states where they are listed under the
  *Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999*. The species, date and
  count stay, but the camera identifiers are replaced, so no one can place the record.
- **Image file names are withheld**, and only images hosted openly by WildObs
  (`filePublic = TRUE`) can be downloaded.
- **Embargoed projects** show their metadata only, as above.


``` r
# one of your open projects, as the public receives it
dp <- wildobs_dp_download(api_key = api_key,
                          project_ids = "ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001")[[1]]
obs <- frictionless::read_resource(dp, "observations")

# your records that the public cannot place on a camera, by listing category and species
obscured <- obs[grepl("^obscured_for_", obs$deploymentID), ]
table(obscured$scientificName, obscured$deploymentID)
#>                      
#>                       obscured_for_endangered_species
#>   Casuarius casuarius                             413
#>   Dasyurus maculatus                               39
```

## How you will be cited

Every project carries the citation you agreed to, ending with its
[RAiD](https://raid.org), a persistent identifier for your research activity. Anyone using
`cite_datapackages()` receives it with the database version they downloaded, so you can
search for your RAiD to find where your data were used:


``` r
writeLines(cite_datapackages(meta))
#> Zachary Amir & Annabel Smith (2023). WildObs Camera Trap Data Package: UQ's undergraduate widlife techonologies camera trapping module comparing human and AI comptuer vision [Camera Trap Data Package]. WildObs National Wildlife Camera Database. https://wildobs.org.au. RAiD: https://raid.org/10.83062/a3efd562. WildObs database version 1.0.1.
#> Zachary Amir, Linda Behrendorff & Matthew Luskin (2022). WildObs Camera Trap Data Package: UQ & QPWS collaboration to study impacts of 2019-20 bushfires on K'gari's long-nosed potoroos [Camera Trap Data Package]. WildObs National Wildlife Camera Database. https://wildobs.org.au. RAiD: https://raid.org/10.83062/ba8f4587. WildObs database version 1.0.2.
#> Zachary Amir, Matthew Luskin & Linda Behrendorff (2023). WildObs Camera Trap Data Package: Camera Trap Module for UQ's BIOL2015 Field Ecology Studies Course from 2023, 2024, 2025 [Camera Trap Data Package]. WildObs National Wildlife Camera Database. https://wildobs.org.au. RAiD: https://raid.org/10.83062/1b8c4374. WildObs database version 2.1.1.
#> Zachary Amir, Tom Bruce & Matthew Luskin (2022). WildObs Camera Trap Data Package: Zachary Amir's camera trap surveys from 6 national parks in QLD's Wet Tropics rainforests from late 2022 to early 2023 targeting feral and native vertebrates [Camera Trap Data Package]. WildObs National Wildlife Camera Database. https://wildobs.org.au. RAiD: https://raid.org/10.83062/cb5829ab. WildObs database version 1.1.1.
```

Papers and datasets that already use a project are listed in its `relatedIdentifiers`:


``` r
related <- extract_metadata(meta, "relatedIdentifiers")
related[related$relatedIdentifierType == "DOI", c("relationType", "relatedIdentifier", "DPID")]
#>      relationType                               relatedIdentifier
#> 6  IsSupplementTo              https://doi.org/10.1002/ece3.71464
#> 8  IsSupplementTo https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2026.181926
#> 9      IsSourceOf                 https://doi.org/10.15468/kjqw3f
#> 10      IsCitedBy         https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19552244
#>                                         DPID
#> 6  ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001
#> 8  ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001
#> 9  ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001
#> 10 ZAmir_QLD_Wet_Tropics_2022_WildObsID_0001
```

To add a publication that uses your data, send its DOI to <support@wildobs.org.au>.
